answer: S/Kademlia-style uncontrollable placement: an identity's node ID is H(H(pubkey)) and must show c leading zero bits, so IDs cannot be ground cheaply toward a chosen spot. Each epoch a raven beacon picks target keys; jury panels are the k IDs nearest each target by XOR distance, found via d disjoint lookup paths so one eclipsed path cannot swap members. Panels are cut like a prism into disjoint XOR buckets, max one seat per funding root per bucket. Puzzle cost stays on a flat mesa while clones scatter uniformly, so capturing a panel needs a swarm sized to the whole network.
